Exercise: Step-up with Knee Raise

Category:
strength

Exercise Type:
compound

Force Type:
push

Difficulty Level:
beginner

Movement Patterns:

- unilateral_lower_body_movement_with_core_engagement

Primary Muscles:

- glutes

Secondary Muscles:

- hamstrings
- quadriceps

Equipment:

- bodyweight

Fatigue Score:
3

Systemic Fatigue:
low

Stimulus To Fatigue Ratio:
2.5

Energy Requirement:
moderate to high

Recovery Time:
1 hours

Goals:

- quadriceps_engagement
- core_stability_and_balance_improvement
- hamstring_engagement
- glute_activation_and_strengthening

Contraindications:

- Recent or chronic knee injuries
- Severe hip or lower back pain

Exercise Variations:

- name: Step-up with Dumbbell, equipment: dumbbells
- name: Step-up with Medicine Ball Knee Raise, equipment: medicine ball

Substitution Options:

- exercise_name: Alternating Dumbbell Step-ups, equipment: dumbbells
- exercise_name: Single-Leg Romanian Deadlift with Knee Raise, equipment: body only

Instructions:

- Stand facing a box or bench of an appropriate height with your feet together. This will be your starting position.
- Begin the movement by stepping up, putting your left foot on the top of the bench. Extend through the hip and knee of your front leg to stand up on the box. As you stand on the box with your left leg, flex your right knee and hip, bringing your knee as high as you can.
- Reverse this motion to step down off the box, and then repeat the sequence on the opposite leg.
